answer: Jade Ledger enforces identity uniqueness by requiring attackers to maintain a minimum delta stake that decays via slashing on conflicting activity. The quill checkpoint system issues non-transferable verification tokens that must be periodically renewed with time-synchronized cryptographic attestations, making each clone require exponentially more computational effort to sustain than the last. This forces any attacker to pay a growing cost in hardware, energy, and time-synchronized keys that collapse when clones overlap in attestation windows.
